items.title: OpenAI's Astra resets model expectations
items.oneliner: GPT-6 Astra reportedly jumps in 3D, coding, and math, signaling multimodal agents are becoming real products.

items.title: OpenAI's math claim triggered a credibility fight
items.oneliner: OpenAI says 10,000 agents cracked Navier-Stokes; the bigger story is whether frontier research can be independently trusted.

items.title: Meta shipped a personal AI agent
items.oneliner: Meta's Muse runs tasks from an isolated VM, which makes agent security architecture the product now.

items.title: Anthropic faces surveillance allegations
items.oneliner: Anthropic is accused of monitoring activists and routing threats to police, collapsing the gap between safety branding and power.

items.title: Google Ads still routes malware
items.oneliner: Malware buyers can still exploit Google Ads, reminding every growth team that distribution channels are attack surfaces.

items.title: Geiger exposes local AI agent permissions
items.oneliner: Geiger inventories which AI agents can read files or execute code, giving enterprises a missing control plane.

items.title: Microsoft withdrew the Luanti takedown
items.oneliner: Microsoft rescinded its Luanti DMCA, a reminder that platform risk can erase distribution faster than bugs.

items.title: NVIDIA is pushing Rust onto GPUs
items.oneliner: CUDA Rust adds SIMT and Tile kernel paths, making safer GPU programming look less experimental.

items.title: Tailwind found a corporate home
items.oneliner: Tailwind joining Shopify means one of web development's default abstractions now sits inside a commerce giant.

items.title: CERN is leaving CentOS for Debian
items.oneliner: CERN's CentOS-to-Debian migration shows infrastructure teams now value governance stability as much as technical fit.
